newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Cycle & Carriage on diversification trail.
newsitem.headline: Cycle & Carriage on diversification trail.

text.p: Singapore's Cycle & Carriage Ltd plans to diversify its property and motor retail business in Asia with one new core business in the near future, a company spokeswoman said on Wednesday.
She said the group plans to start bus building and is seeking a partner to assemble Mercedes-Benz buses in Malaysia.

Managing director Philip Eng earlier told The Business Times newspaper, "We're looking at other complementary busineses." He said a business development manager had been hired to seek fresh opportunities in the region.
Eng said property development, which accounts for a third of the group's pre-tax profits, will figure more prominently.

He said he was confident of Cycle & Carriage's performance in the sector despite the property downturn in Singapore this year. Property prices have eased off since the government introduced anti-speculation measures in May.

Cycle & Carriage-owned Malayan Credit plans to launch its Spring Bloom development project in Lorong Chuan, central Singapore early next year. In the longer term, it plans to join the land from collective bungalow purchases with Habitat Properties to build a luxury condominium development.
